scope: Independent review of the Colab runtime, notebook, scaled-data release builder, publication gate, scale pipeline, CPU recovery check, focused tests, and retained review evidence. Verified all 27 file hashes in the actual prepared-v3-1000 manifest. Ran load_release on the actual prepared files by substituting local paths for hf_hub_download. It accepted exactly 1000 train, 100 dev, and 84 validation rows. This used no remote v3 release.

Matched every one of the 1184 selected metadata records to its retained exact-row review. All input, output, pair, and overall verdicts were pass. The runtime checked row schemas, guide targets and required context, unique source identities, source-group separation, and the two fixed v2 validation hashes. Canonical mode system prompts were also checked directly.

Encoded all 1184 actual SFT rows with the cached pinned Liquid tokenizer and encode_example. Prompt labels and the trailing chat newline were masked, assistant text and its EOS were supervised, and no row required truncation. Maximum full chat length was 4029 tokens. Maximum prompt length plus the 2048-token generation reserve was 4091. The 16-row proof selection and 1000 distinct training source groups were verified.

Inspected Transformers 5.21.0 checkpoint save, rotation, restore, and best-model selection code. The recovery callback runs after a complete local checkpoint save and rotation. Rotation retains the latest and best checkpoints, and the stable run-bound local directory preserves the absolute best-checkpoint path stored by Trainer.

Ran a temporary native random LFM CPU probe with the pinned tokenizer, two existing v2 rows, the production collator, make_trainer, and recovery callback. It interrupted after optimizer step 2 while step 1 remained the best checkpoint. After deleting local scratch, restore_recovery restored step 2 with optimizer state and step 1 with model files but no optimizer copy. Training resumed through step 3. Trainer selected step 1, and both the selected and reloaded model parameters exactly matched the earlier best weights. Persistent storage still contained exactly two recovery archives. Existing CPU integration outputs were not changed.

Loaded the pinned base generation config from the local cache into the temporary tiny model before trainer construction. The clean greedy config saved successfully with checkpoints. A direct Transformers _prepare_generation_config probe returned exactly the recorded explicit config.

Verified that the retained CPU integration receipt matches the exact current runtime SHA256 and reports two optimizer steps, restored continuation through step 2, a nonzero parameter update, and reloaded model loss. This review's temporary probe independently exercised recovery with different best and latest checkpoints.

Confirmed that audit_publication rejects the actual local_data_selection_only preparation before it can publish. Inspected the final builder's exact passing Sol script/notebook gate and exact CPU recovery-evidence gate. Focused tests rejected stale hashes, a failed verdict, and an Opus implementation approval.

Compiled every notebook Python cell and verified that saved outputs are empty. The notebook pins its training packages, retains the Colab CUDA torch installation, records package and session environment reports, uses the same frozen validation inputs and explicit greedy runtime for baseline and tuned outputs, and leaves semantic comparison to a later judged evaluation.
limitations: This is an implementation approval for the exact script and notebook hashes above. It is not evidence that the actual 230M student trains successfully or improves rewrite quality.

No actual 230M weights were loaded or trained. No L4 GPU, BF16 autocast, Colab runtime, Drive FUSE, Drive quota, network interruption, or GPU memory/throughput execution was performed. CPU probes used a random 2080592-parameter native LFM. Drive and local-space thresholds remain unverified on Colab.

The full baseline, proof, train, and tuned main paths were not executed end to end. The temporary Trainer probe used short existing rows, a three-step CPU schedule, and a callback that supplied increasing selection losses to force a distinct older best checkpoint.

No new v3 Hub upload or private Hub download was performed. The real-row runtime check substituted local files for Hub downloads. The final release builder and remote publication were inspected, but were not executed in this review.

This review did not repeat the semantic review of data rows. Retained Opus verdicts are model judgments. They do not supply human labels, human calibration, or an unseen final test. Source-group and text-overlap checks do not prove the absence of every semantic relationship.
No new model/API calls, data generation, example edits, implementation edits, notebook edits, or test edits were performed. Personal holdouts and credentials were not inspected.
